articles.title: DARE–ICAR Intensifies Special Campaign 6.0, Promotes Cleanliness, Sustainable Waste Management and Better Office Spaces Across Institutes
articles.full_content:
Department of Agricultural Research/Indian Council of Agricultural Research has been observing Special Campaign 6.0 through focused cleanliness and office-space improvement activities, segregation and responsible handling of waste, reuse of usable materials, and awareness activities involving staff, farmers and local stakeholders, wherever undertaken.
Activities also include record management, digitization, plantation and environment-friendly practices, cleanliness campaigns in all branches throughout the country, citizen-centric practices, scrap disposal, electronic waste management, enhancement of office space, etc. the institutes are continuously identifying black spots in and around its premises and striving to make them clean. Officials in the institute campuses are also conducting awareness camps for making all aware about the value of swacchata.
In several campuses free medical camps were also arranged. Felicitation of safaimitras have also been a continuing practice. Participation of all levels of officials in swachhata activities is praiseworthy, both inside the office premises as well as in outside area of the campuses. Extensive cleaning drive has been carried in the farm and fields as well as roads surrounding the campuses. Particular attention was given to keeping metal, plastic waste separate from general waste thereby improving cleanliness, organization, and waste-management practices.The corridors were particularly cleared and organized, resulting in a cleaner and more orderly working environment. The swachhata special campaign 6 activity has promoted responsible waste management and maintaining hygiene around the working place.

India’s Social Security Coverage
articles.full_content:
Strengthening Worker Protection
India’s social security framework has expanded through wider EPFO coverage, digital reforms and welfare initiatives. EPFO provides provident fund savings, pension and insurance benefits to eligible members. The increase in the mandatory coverage wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 is expected to bring over 51 lakh additional employees within its ambit. Digital initiatives aim to simplify registration, withdrawals and claim settlement. Beyond EPFO, initiatives such as e-Shram, and schemes like PM-SYM and the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana extend support to unorganised workers and vulnerable groups. These measures strengthen access to social protection across employment categories and stages of life.
Social Security as a Pillar of Worker Protection
As economies evolve, employment patterns and sources of livelihood continue to change. The expansion of informal, gig and platform-based work, along with variations in income and employment continuity, makes social security increasingly important for workers and their families. Social security provides protection against income loss and other contingencies across different stages of life. It also strengthens financial security during retirement and periods of vulnerability.
India has significantly expanded the reach of social protection in recent years. Social protection coverage increased from 19% in 2015 to 68.4% in 2026 . This expansion has brought more than one billion people within the social protection framework.
For Indian workers, social security provides financial security beyond their working years. The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) plays an important role by administering provident fund, pension and insurance schemes for eligible workers. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment and one of the world’s largest social security institutions . Its schemes help workers build retirement savings, access pension benefits and secure financial support for their families.
Three Pillars of EPFO-led Social Security
EPFO social security architecture includes provident fund savings, pension benefits and insurance protection.
• Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 (EPF) The new EPF 2026 introduced under the Social Security Code, 2020 (Code) replaced the erstwhile Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 2026. The EPF 2026 enables members to build retirement savings through contributions and accrued interest. It also permits partial withdrawals for specified purposes, including housing, higher education, marriage and medical treatment, subject to prescribed conditions.
• Employees’ Pension Scheme, 2026 (EPS) The new EPS 2026 under the Code replaced the erstwhile Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995. The EPS 2026 provides monthly pension benefits to eligible members on superannuation, retirement or disability. It also provides pension benefits to eligible dependents of deceased members, including spouses, children and other eligible famil

EPFO provides provident fund savings, pension and insurance benefits to eligible members. The increase in the mandatory coverage wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 is expected to bring over 51 lakh additional employees within its ambit.

DGFT to Organise State-Level Workshop on Effective Utilisation of Free Trade Agreements in Hyderabad
articles.full_content:
The Office of the Additional Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Hyderabad, in collaboration with the Government of Telangana, is organising a state-level workshop on leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) on November 2, 2026, at T-Hub Knowledge City, Madhapur, Hyderabad.
The workshop aims to enhance awareness and facilitate the effective utilisation of India’s FTAs, with a focus on expanding market access, identifying emerging export opportunities and strengthening Telangana’s export competitiveness.
The Mega FTA Outreach Programme will commence at 3:00 PM and is expected to bring together nearly 200 participants, including leading exporters from Telangana, officials from the District Industries Centres (DICs), representatives of Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), senior officials from the Government of India and the Government of Telangana, and other stakeholders from the trade and industry ecosystem.
The programme will feature dedicated sectoral breakout sessions focusing on key export-oriented sectors, including pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles, and gems and jewellery. Discussions will also cover opportunities and practical interventions across agriculture, dairy, marine products and food processing; textiles, apparel and made-ups; engineering, electronics and semiconductors; and services.
The sessions are expected to facilitate interaction between policymakers, industry representatives and exporters, enabling the identification of sector-specific opportunities, addressing challenges in FTA utilisation and recommending practical measures to improve export performance.
Through this outreach initiative, DGFT seeks to strengthen stakeholder awareness, promote the effective utilisation of India’s FTAs and facilitate greater integration of Telangana’s industries with international markets. The programme is expected to support the state’s export growth by enabling businesses to leverage preferential market access and emerging opportunities under India’s recently signed Free Trade Agreements.

Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and its organisations successfully conclude Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Disposal of Scrap and E-waste results in freeing up 32,854 sq. ft. of space; Revenue worth over Rs. 64.18 lakhs generated
The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), along with its organisations, has successfully undertaken the Special Campaign 6. It concluded today with a renewed commitment to institutionalise Swachhata and minimising pendency within the Ministry and its offices across the country. A key area of focus during this year’s Campaign has been the ‘Effective collection, segregation and disposal of E-waste’, as per guidelines issued by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) on 13.08.2026. The Campaign was undertaken across all 132 identified locations of the Ministry including its Subordinate Offices, Autonomous Bodies, etc.
Special emphasis was laid on disposal of E-waste following due process, as per the provisions contained in the guidelines and SOP issued by DARPG. The activities underscored the importance of environmentally responsible waste management and sustainable administrative practices. The disposal of e-waste including scrap and redundant items resulted in the generation of revenue amounting to Rs. 64,18,158/- and reclamation of 32,854 sq. ft. of valuable office space.
Earlier, during the implementation phase, the Secretary (MoEFCC) undertook a comprehensive inspection of the premises of the Ministry at Indira Paryavaran Bhavan, New Delhi to review the status of collection and segregation of E-waste, scrap and redundant items stored. Emphasizing the importance of environmentally sound and responsible E-waste and other waste management, the Secretary directed that all segregated items be disposed of in a safe and scientific manner through CPCB registered E-waste recyclers, refurbishers and producers, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines.
Secretary, MoEFCC, visited the Ministry premises to review the progress of #SpecialCampaign6. The review covered key activities related to cleanliness, record management and e-waste disposal as part of the ongoing campaign. https://t.co/VF8t7zfVqt
Under various Parameters of Special Campaign 6, 100 per cent achievement has been recorded in the Cleanliness Campaign covering all 132 identified locations. The Ministry also achieved 100 per cent disposal of State Government References, Public Grievance Appeals, PMO References along with the prescribed targets for the review of Physical Files and E-files. Delhi Records Lowest Average AQI for October in the Last Eight Years at 166
articles.full_content:
Delhi Records 220 Good to Moderate AQI Days During January–October 2026, Highest Since 2018 (except 2020)
The monthly average AQI of Delhi for October in 2026 is recorded as 166, against the monthly average AQI for October as 223 in 2025, 234 in 2024, 219 in 2023, 210 in 2022, 173 in 2021, 265 in 2020, 234 in 2019 and 269 in 2018, respectively.
The average AQI of Delhi for the period 01-Jan to 31-Oct is recorded as 167, against the average AQI of 170 in 2025, 184 in 2024, 172 in 2023, 187 in 2022, 179 in 2021, 156 in 2020, 192 in 2019 and 201 in 2018, respectively.
The average PM2.5 concentrations for period 01-Jan to 29-Oct is recorded as 69 µg/m³, against the average concentration of 72 µg/m³ in 2025, 83 µg/m³ in 2024, 76 µg/m³ in 2023, 81 µg/m³ in 2022, 82 µg/m³ in 2021, 71 µg/m³ in 2020, 88 µg/m³ in 2019 and 93 µg/m³ in 2018, during the same period respectively.
The average PM10 concentrations for period 01-Jan to 29-Oct is recorded as 171 µg/m³, against the average concentration of 166 µg/m³ in 2025, 186 µg/m³ in 2024, 174 µg/m³ in 2023, 191 µg/m³ in 2022, 182 µg/m³ in 2021, 147 µg/m³ in 2020, 197 µg/m³ in 2019 and 216 µg/m³ in 2018, during the same period respectively.
The period (January – October) in 2026 witnessed 220 'Good to Moderate' category days (daily average AQI less than 200), against the number of such days being 200 in 2025, 201 in 2024, 206 in 2023, 160 in 2022, 197 in 2021, 224 in 2020, 175 in 2019 and 157 in 2018, respectively.
The period (January – October) in 2026 witnessed 84 ‘Poor to Severe+’ category days (daily average AQI more than 200), against the number of such days being 104 in 2025, 104 in 2024, 98 in 2023, 144 in 2022, 107 in 2021, 81 in 2020, 129 in 2019 and 147 in 2018, respectively.
CAQM is working closely with various stakeholders concerned to take effective measures for prevention, control and abatement of air pollution and to improve the air quality in Delhi-NCR. These efforts would be intensified with an endeavour to further improve upon the air quality scenario in Delhi-NCR in the coming days.

24th Instalment of PM-KISAN
articles.full_content:
Direct Benefit Transfer of over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers
PM-KISAN provides eligible farmer families ₹ 6,000 annually in three instalments , supporting agricultural investments and household financial stability . The 24 th instalment transferred over ₹ 18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers, taking cumulative disbursements beyond ₹ 4.64 lakh crore . Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, Direct Benefit Transfer, e-KYC and digital verification strengthen transparency and reduce intermediaries. The scheme’s continuation until 2030-31, backed by a ₹ 3.15 lakh crore financial outlay, reinforces sustained support for farmer income security.
PM-KISAN: Strengthening Income Security for Farmers
The government has released the 24 th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) on 30 October 2026, at Banaskantha, Gujarat . More than 9.34 crore eligible farmers received around ₹ 18,690 crore in direct financial assistance. The funds were transferred through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system , ensuring transparency and eliminating intermediaries. The scheme is widely regarded as a significant initiative towards ensuring ‘ Annadata Samman’ .
Recently, in July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved continuation of the PM-KISAN Scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial outlay of ₹ 3.15 lakh crore has been approved for the scheme during this period. The approval reiterates the government’s commitment that the prosperity of farmers forms the foundation of the nation’s prosperity.
Direct Income Support to Small and Marginal Farmers under PM-KISAN
PM-KISAN is a centrally sponsored scheme launched on February 24, 2019. The scheme seeks to provide assured income support to landholding farmer families nationwide with cultivable land. Under the scheme, each eligible farmer family receives annual financial assistance of ₹6,000 . This is disbursed in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts .
The assistance provided under PM-KISAN has enabled farmers to make timely investments in seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, agricultural machinery and other agricultural requirements. This has enhanced farmers’ productive capacity , reduced their dependence on informal credit and strengthened the financial stability of rural households .
So far, more than ₹ 4.64 lakh crore has been disbursed to eligible farmer families across the country through 24 instalments. The scheme benefits are provided to farmers after their land records are seeded on the PM-KISAN portal. They also must link their bank accounts to Aadhaar and complete e-KYC verification . Reflecting the government’s continued commitment to strengthening farmers’ income security, the Union Budget 2026-27 has allocated ₹ 60,000 crore for the PM-KISAN scheme.
The scheme seeks to increase the income of small and marginal farmers by providing financial support for agricultural inputs. This helps in improving crop health and productivity . Providing direct financial assistance

ICAR–NBAIR, Bengaluru Streams of 24th instalment of PM-KISAN event and Distributes Biocontrol Inputs under the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes
articles.full_content:
ICAR–NBAIR, Bengaluru organized the live webcast of the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)’ programme addressed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi for the benefit of farmers particularly Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) on October 30, 2026, at ICAR-NBAIR, Yelahanka campus. The event was graced by Dr. Y.N. Shivalingaiah Hon’ble Dean (Agri.), University of Agricultural Sciences, GKVK, Bengaluru, as the Chief Guest, in the presence of Dr. T. Venkatesan, Director, ICAR–NBAIR.
In his opening remarks Dr. T. Venkatesan briefed the dignitaries and participants about the various activities of ICAR-NBAIR and the role of the institute in supporting farmers by the development of various biological control technologies for the successful pest management. He advocated the farmers for the adoption of eco-friendly methods to restore the soil health and created awareness about the need for sustainable agriculture.
Chief Guest Dr. Y.N. Shivalingaiah highlighted the importance of PM-KISAN flagship programme, wherein Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi released the 24 th instalment of ₹18,690.32 crore Samman Rashi directly to the bank accounts of more than 9.34 crore eligible farmers via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from Banaskantha, Gujarat.
In his address, he stated that the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is keen to improve the prosperity of farmers in our country. He emphasised the importance of crop rotation, integrated nutrient and pest management. He advised farmers to use biocontrol agents and bio-rational technologies for the successful management of pest and disease control for sustainable agriculture.
The virtual event marking the release of the 24 th instalment of the PM-KISAN Scheme by the Prime Minister was witnessed by 150 people including 113 farmers, besides students and researchers. As part of the programme, biocontrol inputs were distributed to farmers from Kolar District of Karnataka under the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC).

Shivalingaiah Hon’ble Dean (Agri.), University of Agricultural Sciences, GKVK, Bengaluru, as the Chief Guest, in the presence of Dr. Venkatesan briefed the dignitaries and participants about the various activities of ICAR-NBAIR and the role of the institute in supporting farmers by the development of various biological control technologies for the successful pest management.

ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids, Pakyong joins the Nation in celebrating PM-KISAN Utsav Diwas
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi today released the 24th instalment of Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) from Banaskantha, Gujarat, transferring more than Rs. 18,690 crore directly to the bank accounts of over 9.34 crore farmers across the country through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). On the occasion, the Prime Minister also dedicated to the nation 521 units developed under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and inaugurated 12 Horticulture Clusters.
Joining the nationwide celebration, ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids (NRCO), Pakyong organized “PM-KISAN Utsav” with organic farmers of Pakyong District.
A total of 85 farmers/beneficiaries from Ganchung, Damlakha, Taza, Pachak, Parkha, Kabuthang, Taksang, Mamjey, Yakten, Pakyong, Chalamthung, Pachey, Kartok and Namcheybong villages of Pakyong District participated in the programme and witnessed the live telecast of the Prime Minister’s address.
The PM-KISAN scheme, a Central Sector Scheme launched on 24th February 2019, aims to provide financial support to all landholding farmer families with cultivable land. Under the scheme, eligible farmers receive Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000 each. Farmers can self-register through the PM-Kisan portal, mobile application and Common Service Centres, with land records digitally verified and the amount transferred directly to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts through DBT, ensuring transparency and timely delivery.
As one of the world’s largest DBT programmes, PM-KISAN has significantly impacted farmers by providing direct financial support. Notably, around 25% of the total benefits go to women beneficiaries. Women farmers have received more than Rs. 1.06 lakh crore under PM-KISAN till the 23rd instalment, with nearly one out of every four beneficiaries being a woman farmer, reflecting the Government’s commitment to empowering women farmers and enhancing their economic security.
The programme at ICAR-NRCO, Pakyong was organized under the leadership of Dr. S.P. Das, Director, and coordinated by Dr. L.C. De, Nodal Officer, with support from Scientists Dr. N.S. Kalaivanan, Dr. Nikhila V.A. and Dr. T. Rihne, along with Administrative, Financial, Technical, Supporting staff, Young Professionals and Contractual staff.
The programme evoked a positive response from the farmers and beneficiaries of Pakyong District.

Farmers’ Day Celebrations and PM-KISAN Utsav Diwas Held at ICAR–IIRR, Rajendranagar
articles.full_content:
Union Minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar Calls for Innovative Research to Enhance Farm Productivity
Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar urged agricultural researchers to develop new crop varieties through innovative ideas, improved practices and modern technology to help farmers achieve higher yields with lower investments, while conserving the environment and protecting human health. The Minister attended the Farmers’ Day celebrations as the Chief Guest at the ICAR–Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR–IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, which also featured PM-KISAN Utsav Diwas marking the release of the 24th instalment of the PM-KISAN scheme. Addressing the gathering, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar highlighted the pivotal role of farmers in realising the Prime Minister’s vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. He described ICAR as an important institution for Telangana, recognising its significant contributions to agricultural research. He noted that research institutions like ICAR have been developing new crop varieties to help farmers cultivate crops more effectively and minimise losses.
Expressing concern over the challenges and stress faced by farmers across the country, the Minister emphasised the need for continued research and innovation to address their concerns. Highlighting the role of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme in providing financial assistance to farmers, he stressed the importance of ensuring that all eligible beneficiaries receive the benefits of government welfare schemes. On the occasion, the Minister encouraged farmers to follow the guidance and recommendations of ICAR–IIRR scientists and researchers. He emphasised that adopting scientific advice and improved agricultural practices would help farmers enhance productivity and increase their yields.
In his opening remarks, Dr. M. Srinivas Prasad, Director, ICAR–IIRR, highlighted the research initiatives undertaken by the Institute in the field of agriculture to help farmers enhance agricultural productivity, improve crop health and increase their income. This was followed by an interactive session between farmers and scientists, during which ICAR–IIRR scientists showcased their latest innovations, including newly developed rice varieties, and briefed farmers on the appropriate use of pesticides. The scientists also addressed various queries raised by the farmers and provided necessary clarifications. Smt. M. Jayasree, NGO representative of Prakriti Environment Society (PES), Dr. M. Srinivas Prasad, Director, ICAR–IIRR, other dignitaries from ICAR–IIRR and around 200 farmers participated in the event.

articles.title: DGFT Chennai Organises State-Level Workshop on Leveraging Free Trade Agreements to Boost Exports from Tamil Nadu
articles.full_content:
Workshop Highlights India's Vision of Becoming a US$30 Trillion Economy by 2047
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, in collaboration with Guidance Tamil Nadu, Government of Tamil Nadu, and the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO), organised a State-Level Workshop on “Leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs)” to enhance awareness of international trade opportunities and strengthen the export competitiveness of Tamil Nadu.
The workshop highlighted the significant market opportunities arising from India's nine new Free Trade Agreements, covering economies with a combined Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of approximately US$60 trillion. The discussions emphasised the importance of leveraging these agreements to expand India's global trade presence, strengthen exports and work towards the US$1 trillion export target for the current year, while contributing to the vision of a US$30 trillion Indian economy by 2047.
A total of 198 exporters representing nine sectors, including engineering, leather, gems and jewellery, and agriculture, participated in the workshop. Representatives from MSMEs, Export Promotion Councils, Chambers of Commerce and other stakeholders attended the programme.
Smt. Rajalakshmi Devraj, Additional Director General of Foreign Trade, Regional Authority, Chennai, highlighted the substantial economic opportunities created by India's nine new FTAs. She stated that these agreements provide access to international markets representing approximately US$60 trillion in combined GDP, offering significant potential for Indian exporters across various sectors.
She emphasised the importance of enhancing India's export performance and highlighted the US$1 trillion export target for the current year, alongside the long-term vision of building a US$30 trillion economy by 2047. She encouraged exporters to effectively utilise preferential market access under FTAs and leverage the Government of India's Export Promotion Mission to strengthen their international presence and competitiveness.
Placing special emphasis on agriculture, Smt. Rajalakshmi Devraj noted that nine Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) from various districts of Tamil Nadu had participated in the workshop. She highlighted the importance of enabling agricultural producers to explore international markets and benefit from emerging export opportunities.
She also observed that the participation of exporters from diverse sectors provided an opportunity for networking, exchange of experiences and identification of new business prospects.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Alex Paul Menon, Development Commissioner, MEPZ Special Economic Zone, highlighted Tamil Nadu's pioneering role in India's export sector and stressed the importance of enabling exporters to take full advantage of emerging international trade opportunities. articles.full_content:
The ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Umiam, in collaboration with the District Agriculture Office, Ri-Bhoi, and ICAR-Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Ri-Bhoi, organised a live-streaming programme on the release of the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme. A total of 105 farmers from different villages of Ri-Bhoi district, including 31 male and 74 female farmers, participated in the programme.
The event provided farmers an opportunity to witness the nationwide release of the instalment and understand the benefits of the scheme, which provides eligible farmer families with financial assistance of ₹6,000 annually through Direct Benefit Transfer in three instalments.
Addressing the farmers, Dr. G. Kadirvel, Director, ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, encouraged the farmers to make the best use of various government schemes, including PM-KISAN, PMFBY and PM-KUSUM. He highlighted that such initiatives, along with scientific farming practices, can help farmers reduce risks and improve their livelihoods.
Smt. Serolyne Chyne, District Agriculture Officer, Ri-Bhoi, encouraged farmers to stay connected with the Agriculture Department and actively participate in its programmes. She also stressed the importance of completing essential formalities such as e-KYC, Aadhaar seeding and bank account verification to receive scheme benefits without any difficulty.
Dr. Mokidul Islam, Principal Scientist and Head, ICAR-KVK Ri-Bhoi, highlighted the importance of PM-KISAN in providing financial support to farming families, particularly small and marginal farmers. He also emphasised the role of KVK in helping farmers adopt improved agricultural practices through training, technical guidance and demonstrations.
The participation of 74 women farmers was a special highlight of the programme, recognising the important role women play in agriculture and rural livelihoods. The programme concluded with a renewed emphasis on connecting farmers with government support schemes, scientific knowledge and opportunities for better and more sustainable livelihoods.

The live telecast of the national programme marking the release of the 24th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme was organised at the ICAR–National Institute of Biotic Stress Management, Raipur. Farmers at the institute witnessed the programme held at Banaskantha, Gujarat, where the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, released the financial assistance directly into the bank accounts of farmers across the country.
Before the live telecast and the Prime Minister’s address, Director of the Institute, Dr. P. K. Rai, addressed the farmers. He highlighted the objectives and significance of the PM-KISAN scheme and elaborated on various initiatives undertaken by the Government of India for agricultural development and farmers’ welfare. He encouraged farmers to avail themselves of the benefits of government schemes and adopt scientific agricultural practices to enhance farm productivity and sustainability.

He emphasised that the PM-KISAN scheme has become an integral part of the lives of millions of farming families and that financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) is helping farmers meet their agricultural and household needs.

He particularly emphasised crop diversification and advised farmers to integrate pulses and oilseed crops into their existing cropping systems, diversify traditional cropping patterns and make efficient use of available agricultural resources.

Local representatives, including Shri Santosh Kurre, Sarpanch of Beltukri village; Shri Bhuvneshwar Khunte from Kurra village; and Shri Dushyant Sahu from Bitia village, were also present.
The programme witnessed active participation and enthusiastic interaction among farmers. The event provided an important platform to disseminate information about various farmer-welfare initiatives of the Government of India and to promote scientific agricultural technologies, crop diversification and sustainable farming practices. Scientists, officers, and other staff members of the Institute were also present. The programme was effectively coordinated and conducted by Dr. K. C. Sharma and Dr. Priyanka Meena.
